topics.title: Desktop, Start and windows
topics.md:
The desktop starts with a few icons: **File Commander**, **Recycle Bin**, **ANIMA** and **Help**. Every other app is in the **Start** menu.

## Start
- The button at the left of the taskbar opens Start. Type straight away to search apps, files and settings.
- **Pinned** shows the apps you pinned. **All apps** lists them by category: tap a category to see only that one.
- At the bottom of Start: your name (or the device's), the **Settings** button and the **power** button (lock, sign out, restart where the device allows it).

## Windows
- Drag the title bar to move a window; drag it to a screen edge to snap it.
- The ✕ closes it, and so does `Ctrl` + `W`. `Esc` never closes a window: it closes system menus and panels.
- `Alt` + `Tab` switches between windows.

## Taskbar
Open apps show in the taskbar. Right-click an app in Start to pin it to the taskbar, to Start or to the desktop.

topics.title: Apps and the Store
topics.md:
## Where the apps are
Every installed app is in **Start › All apps**, by category: System, Productivity, Photos music and video, Games, Tools, Network and messaging.

## An app on the desktop
Right-click (or press and hold) an app in Start, then **Add to desktop**. The same menu removes it from the desktop or pins it to Start or the taskbar.

## The Store
Open **Store** from Start for more apps. Every package is signed, and the system checks the signature before installing it and, where needed, before every launch. The Store only shows apps that suit this device.

To remove an app installed from the Store: right-click it in Start, then **Uninstall**. System apps cannot be uninstalled.

topics.title: Files and the Recycle Bin
topics.md:
## File Commander
**File Commander** is the file manager: folders, copy, move, rename, previews. Opening a file hands it to the app associated with its type.

## The Recycle Bin
- A file deleted in File Commander or on the desktop goes to the **Recycle Bin**, where you can restore it to its folder.
- The Recycle Bin keeps the last 20 items: when a new one arrives, the oldest is deleted for good.
- A folder deleted in File Commander does not go through the Recycle Bin: the system tells you before doing it.
- In the Recycle Bin you can **Restore** one item or all of them, or **Empty bin** (it cannot be undone).

The Recycle Bin icon always stays on the desktop: it cannot be removed.

topics.title: Settings
topics.md:
Open **Settings** with the gear button at the bottom of Start, or from Start › All apps.

- **Appearance**: light or dark theme, wallpaper, icon size.
- **Network**: the device's connections, where it can manage them.
- **AI / Models**: providers and keys for ANIMA, or a model that runs in the browser.
- **Accounts**: the people who use the device, where there can be more than one.
- **Updates**: the installed version and new ones.
- **About**: the device, the version, the space.

The language is changed in Settings and is the same for the whole system and every app.

topics.title: Keyboard shortcuts
topics.md:
## System
- `Win` (pressed alone): opens or closes Start
- `Ctrl` + `Space`: ANIMA, from anywhere
- `Alt` + `Tab`: switches between windows
- `Win` + arrows: snaps the active window
- `Ctrl` + `Alt` + `L`: locks the screen
- `Ctrl` + `W`: closes the active window
- `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `V`: clipboard history
- `Esc`: closes system menus and panels

## Desktop
- Arrows: move between icons; `Enter` opens
- `F2`: renames the selected icon
- `Delete`: deletes the selection (files go to the Recycle Bin)
- `Ctrl` + `A`: selects all

## Documents
- `Ctrl` + `S` saves, `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `S` saves as, `Ctrl` + `O` opens, `Ctrl` + `N` new

topics.title: Accounts
topics.md:
Up to five people can work on this device, each with their own account.

## What belongs to each person
Everyone has their own documents, settings, desktop, Recycle Bin and cloud archive. Nobody sees anyone else's files.

## Administrator
The first account is the administrator. In **Settings › Accounts** they create and remove accounts, reset passwords and decide who else is an administrator.

## Signing in and out
- On opening, the system asks for a name and password.
- To sign out: the power button at the bottom of Start › **Sign out**.
- A password set by the administrator must be changed at the first sign-in.

After a few wrong attempts sign-in pauses for a while: it protects passwords from anyone trying to guess them.

topics.title: Encrypted cloud archive
topics.md:
The **/r2** drive in File Commander is your archive in the cloud.

- Files are encrypted in the browser before they leave: the cloud service only sees unreadable data.
- The archive password never leaves the device and cannot be recovered: keep it safe. When you create the archive you get a recovery key.
- With more than one account, each person has a separate archive.
- If someone rolls the archive back to an old version, the system notices and tells you.

topics.title: ANIMA
topics.md:
**ANIMA** is the system assistant. Open it from the desktop, or with `Ctrl` + `Space` from anywhere.

- It answers questions, writes and summarises text, opens apps and files for you.
- It works with an AI provider and your own key (Settings › AI / Models) or with a model that runs in the browser, without your data leaving the computer.
- Before doing anything that changes your files or the device, it asks you to confirm.

topics.title: Updates
topics.md:
**Settings › Updates** shows the installed version and checks for a new one. When there is one, the system tells you and you install it from there.

- An update brings the system, its built-in apps and this manual together: the manual always describes the version you have.
- Store apps update from the Store.
- Your files and settings stay where they are.

topics.title: Games
topics.md:
- **Library** gathers the device's games, with covers and recently played.
- Recent games also show at the top of Start and in the games button of the taskbar.
- Saves stay on the device.

topics.title: Terminal
topics.md:
**Terminal** opens a command line. It is for people who know one: commands act directly on files and on the device, without the protection apps have.

- Where the device offers a system shell, Terminal opens that one: the commands and their manual are the system's.
- Elsewhere Terminal offers NucleoOS's own commands: `help` lists them, `man` followed by a command's name shows its page. The same pages are in this manual under **Terminal commands**, only for the commands this device has.
- `Ctrl` + `C` stops the running command.

commands.title: alias - Give a long command a short name
commands.description: Without arguments it lists the aliases. With name=command it defines one, saved on the card so it survives a reload. On a 56-key thumb keyboard the typing is the cost, which is what makes this worth its bytes.
commands.details:
NAME
  alias - Give a long command a short name

SYNOPSIS
  alias [name=command]

DESCRIPTION
  Without arguments it lists the aliases. With name=command it defines one, saved on the card so it survives a reload. On a 56-key thumb keyboard the typing is the cost, which is what makes this worth its bytes.

OPTIONS
  name=command
    Define an alias.
  name
    Show one alias.

DEVICE COST
  One POST /api/fs/write when an alias changes, into the app's own folder. Nothing at all when a command runs.

NOTES
  An alias expands once, on the command word only, and an alias body containing a pipe, a redirect or ; && || is refused: a saved string must not be able to smuggle in an operator the user never typed.

SEE ALSO
  unalias(1), which(1), export(1)

EXAMPLES
  alias ll='ls /data'
  alias errs='dmesg -l E'
  alias

commands.title: apps - List the installed apps, or open one
commands.description: Prints one tab-separated row per installed app: id, name, whether it is enabled, and its route. With open it asks the shell to launch one.
commands.details:
NAME
  apps - List the installed apps, or open one

SYNOPSIS
  apps [-a]   |   apps open <id>

DESCRIPTION
  Prints one tab-separated row per installed app: id, name, whether it is enabled, and its route. With open it asks the shell to launch one.

OPTIONS
  -a
    Include disabled apps.
  open <id>
    Open that app in the shell.

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/apps, memoised for 30 s. Opening an app is a shell message, not a device call.

NOTES
  This is deliberately NOT a process list. Nothing on the device knows which windows are open, so a ps built on this endpoint would print all 46 installed apps as if they were running.

SEE ALSO
  which(1), assoc(1), open(1)

EXAMPLES
  apps
  apps -a | grep off
  apps open notepad

SYNOPSIS

commands.title: base64 - Encode or decode base64
commands.description: Encodes a file or standard input to base64, or decodes it back with -d. This is the only way a binary blob crosses a text pipeline or the OS clipboard.
commands.details:
NAME
  base64 - Encode or decode base64

SYNOPSIS
  base64 [-d] [file]

DESCRIPTION
  Encodes a file or standard input to base64, or decodes it back with -d. This is the only way a binary blob crosses a text pipeline or the OS clipboard.

OPTIONS
  -d
    Decode instead of encode.
  [file]
    Read this file; without it, read standard input.

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/fs/read when a file is named, and nothing at all in a pipeline.

NOTES
  The encoder works on bytes, not on characters: the browser built-in btoa is latin1-only and would corrupt every byte above 0x7F.

SEE ALSO
  hexdump(1), clip(1), tee(1)

EXAMPLES
  base64 /data/logo.png
  base64 /data/logo.b64 | base64 -d | tee /data/logo.png

commands.title: cat - Display file content
commands.description: Print the text content of a file, or pass piped input through.
commands.details:
NAME
  cat - Display the content of a file.

SYNOPSIS
  cat [file]

DESCRIPTION
  Reads the file from the device's storage and prints it as UTF-8 text, without the final newline. An empty file prints '(empty file)'. Paths under /proc are live system nodes that the device serves as plain text, on devices that have them. Without a file, inside a pipe (for example 'diag | cat'), cat passes its input through unchanged. One file at a time: cat does not join several files.

OPTIONS
  [file]
    The path of the file to show, absolute or relative to the current folder. If omitted, cat prints the input it receives from the pipe.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Reads through the web OS file layer, which calls GET '/api/fs/read?path=<file>' on the device; a /proc path is requested from the device directly. Error messages: 'no such file or directory' when the file does not exist, 'not paired (401)' when this browser is not paired, 'cannot reach the file API' when the device does not answer.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. The file was read and printed.
  1
    The file could not be read (missing, browser not paired, device unreachable or another error).

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  grep(1), head(1), tail(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  cat /system/config/settings.json
  cat logs.txt

commands.title: cd - Change working directory
commands.description: Change the current working directory of the terminal session.
commands.details:
NAME
  cd - Change working directory.

SYNOPSIS
  cd [path]

DESCRIPTION
  Modifies the active context path (CWD) of the terminal. If no path is provided, falls back to the system root '/'.
  To ensure filesystem integrity, the client executes a dry-run check via '/api/fs/list' on the target folder before changing paths. If the check returns 404, the path update is aborted.

OPTIONS
  [path]
    The target folder path (e.g. '..', '/data', 'Pictures').

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Updates the local browser variables 'cwd' and 'envVars.CWD'. Relative paths are normalized to prune '.' and resolve '..' segments prior to executing the safety check.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Directory exists and active path updated.
  1
    Target directory does not exist (failed dry-run check).

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  ls(1), pwd(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  cd /data         # Enters /data
  cd ..            # Moves up one directory tier
  cd               # Resets working directory to root /

EXIT CODES

commands.title: clip - Write to or read the OS clipboard
commands.description: Without arguments it puts standard input on the clipboard; with -o it prints what is on it. This is the pipeline's exit to the rest of the OS, and its entrance.
commands.details:
NAME
  clip - Write to or read the OS clipboard

SYNOPSIS
  clip   |   clip -o

DESCRIPTION
  Without arguments it puts standard input on the clipboard; with -o it prints what is on it. This is the pipeline's exit to the rest of the OS, and its entrance.

OPTIONS
  -o
    Read the clipboard instead of writing it.

DEVICE COST
  None on the device: the clipboard is a shell service, remembered by the OS.

NOTES
  Needs the system.clipboard permission.

SEE ALSO
  tee(1), base64(1), say(1)

EXAMPLES
  stat /data/notes.txt | clip
  clip -o | wc

commands.title: cp - Copy file
commands.description: Copy a file from a source path to a destination path.
commands.details:
NAME
  cp - Copy file.

SYNOPSIS
  cp <source> <dest>

DESCRIPTION
  Copies a file from the source path to the destination path, byte for byte. If the destination already exists, it is replaced. Names with spaces go in double quotes. Prints 'copying <source> to <dest> ...' and then 'copied successfully'.

OPTIONS
  <source>
    The original file path to copy.
  <dest>
    The target path where the copy will be created.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Goes through the web OS file layer, which reads the source and writes the copy (on most devices with '/api/fs/read' and '/api/fs/write'). The write is atomic: the bytes go to a temporary file first, so if the copy fails an existing destination is left as it was. A copy that does not fit in the free space is refused before it starts.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. The copy was completed.
  1
    The copy failed: source not found, not enough space, browser not paired or device unreachable.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  mv(1), rm(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  cp /data/orig.txt /data/dest.txt
  cp "my file.txt" "/data/copy.txt"

commands.title: cpu - Cores, frequency, task count and load
commands.description: Prints what the device reports about its processor, one 'key value' line per field: typically the number of cores, the clock frequency, the running tasks or processes and the load. The fields depend on the device.
commands.details:
NAME
  cpu - Cores, frequency, task count and load

SYNOPSIS
  cpu

DESCRIPTION
  Prints what the device reports about its processor, one 'key value' line per field: typically the number of cores, the clock frequency, the running tasks or processes and the load. The fields depend on the device.

OPTIONS

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/cpu.

SEE ALSO
  heap(1), diag(1), uptime(1)

EXAMPLES

  watch -n 5 cpu

commands.title: curl - HTTP web request
commands.description: Perform an HTTP GET request to a URL and output response content.
commands.details:
NAME
  curl - Fetch HTTP web resource.

SYNOPSIS
  curl <url>

DESCRIPTION
  Performs an HTTP GET request and prints the response payload to the terminal stdout.

OPTIONS
  <url>
    The target web address.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Dispatches a GET request. Subject to CORS restrictions in simulated environments. Runs directly through the ESP-IDF Wi-Fi socket stack (LwIP) on physical devices.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success.
  1
    Network offline, CORS block, or host timeout.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  wget(1), ping(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  curl ipify.org
  curl http://example.com

commands.title: cut - Select fields or columns from each line
commands.description: Keeps only part of every line. Without it the column output of /proc and of the device log is not pipeable.
commands.details:
NAME
  cut - Select fields or columns from each line

SYNOPSIS
  cut -d<char> -f<list>   |   cut -c<from>-<to>

DESCRIPTION
  Keeps only part of every line. Without it the column output of /proc and of the device log is not pipeable.

OPTIONS
  -d C
    Field separator (a tab by default).
  -f LIST
    Which fields to keep: 1, 1,3 or 2-4.
  -c A-B
    Keep characters A to B instead of fields.

DEVICE COST
  None. Entirely browser-side.

SEE ALSO
  grep(1), sort(1)

EXAMPLES
  cat /proc/meminfo | cut -d" " -f1
  apps | cut -f1

commands.title: date - Browser and device date and time
commands.description: Show the date and time of this browser and of the device, and optionally set the device clock.
commands.details:
NAME
  date - Browser and device date and time.

SYNOPSIS
  date [-u] [-s]

DESCRIPTION
  Prints two clocks: 'local', the time of this browser, and 'device', the clock of the device, followed by '(NTP-synced)' when the device has synchronised it over the internet or '(no NTP)' when it has not. Times are shown as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS (ISO 8601) in this browser's time zone. If the device does not report its clock, the second line says 'device clock not reported'.

OPTIONS
  -u
    Show both times in UTC (with a trailing Z).
  -s
    Set the device clock from this browser's clock; useful when the device has not synchronised over NTP. On devices that support it; where there are user accounts it needs an administrator.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Reads the device clock from GET '/api/status' (network.time and network.time_synced). With -s it sends POST '/api/time/set' with the browser's time in seconds. A device whose clock cannot be set answers 'date: not available on this device'.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success.
  1
    Device unreachable, browser not paired or clock not set.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  status(1), uptime(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  date
  date -u
  date -s

commands.title: df - Disk space usage
commands.description: Display the total, used and free space of the device's storage.
commands.details:
NAME
  df - Disk space usage.

SYNOPSIS
  df

DESCRIPTION
  Shows the size of the device's storage, how much is used and how much is free, in a table with the columns Filesystem, Size, Used, Avail, Use% and Mounted on. The storage is shown mounted on /data.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Reads GET '/api/status' (storage.total_bytes and storage.free_bytes); used space is total minus free. If the device reports no mounted storage or does not answer, prints 'df: storage not mounted or unreachable'.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Statistics printed.
  1
    Storage not mounted or device unreachable.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  status(1), free(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  df

commands.title: diag - The whole diagnostic table, one key per line
commands.description: Flattens everything /api/diag reports into 'key value' lines, with nested keys joined by a dot (for example mem.free); yes/no values become 1/0 and lists become comma-separated values. What appears depends on the device: typically memory, CPU, network, uptime and system counters. It is the most pipeable command in the set and the best thing to hand to anima.
commands.details:
NAME
  diag - The whole diagnostic table, one key per line

SYNOPSIS
  diag [key-prefix]

DESCRIPTION
  Flattens everything /api/diag reports into 'key value' lines, with nested keys joined by a dot (for example mem.free); yes/no values become 1/0 and lists become comma-separated values. What appears depends on the device: typically memory, CPU, network, uptime and system counters. It is the most pipeable command in the set and the best thing to hand to anima.

OPTIONS
  [key-prefix]
    Show only keys starting with this, e.g. mem or cpu. If no key matches it prints 'diag: no key starts with ...'.

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/diag, instead of a separate request for each part.

SEE ALSO
  heap(1), cpu(1), status(1), anima(1)

EXAMPLES
  diag
  diag mem
  diag | anima "is the memory ok?"
  diag | tee /data/diag.txt

commands.title: display - Turn the panel on or off
commands.description: Switches the physical display, and prints the brightness the device reports afterwards.
commands.details:
NAME
  display - Turn the panel on or off

SYNOPSIS
  display on | display off

DESCRIPTION
  Switches the physical display, and prints the brightness the device reports afterwards.

OPTIONS
  on
    Panel on.
  off
    Panel off.

DEVICE COST
  One POST /api/display.

NOTES
  Needs the device.display permission. On a 120 mAh budget this is the single biggest lever there is, and until now it was only reachable through Settings.

SEE ALSO
  screen(1), status(1)

EXAMPLES
  display off
  display on

commands.title: dmesg - Print the device's system log
commands.description: Print the recent messages of the device's system log.
commands.details:
NAME
  dmesg - Print the device's system log.

SYNOPSIS
  dmesg [-l E|W|I|D|V]

DESCRIPTION
  Fetches the recent messages of the device's system log and prints them as they are. What the log contains and how far back it goes depend on the device.

OPTIONS
  -l LEVEL
    Ask only for messages of that level or more severe: E (error), W (warning), I (info), D (debug), V (verbose). The device does the filtering; a device that does not support it returns the whole log.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Issues GET '/api/logs' (with '?level=X' when -l is given). Where there are user accounts, the log is reserved to an administrator. Error messages: 'dmesg: not paired (401)', 'dmesg: failed to read logs (status N)', 'dmesg: device unreachable'.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Logs printed.
  1
    Browser not paired, request refused or device unreachable.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  status(1), reboot(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  dmesg
  dmesg -l W
  dmesg | grep wifi

commands.title: du - Disk usage per directory, biggest first
commands.description: Walks a subtree and adds up the size of the files in each directory, rolling children into their parents. The output is sorted by size, so the answer to "what is eating the card" is the first line.
commands.details:
NAME
  du - Disk usage per directory, biggest first

SYNOPSIS
  du [-d N] [path]

DESCRIPTION
  Walks a subtree and adds up the size of the files in each directory, rolling children into their parents. The output is sorted by size, so the answer to "what is eating the card" is the first line.

OPTIONS
  -d N
    Descend at most N levels (default 2, hard maximum 6).
  [path]
    Where to start; the working directory by default.

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/fs/list per directory, strictly sequential, and never more than 60 in one invocation. Ctrl+C stops it.

NOTES
  A listing costs the device a stat() per entry, so the walk is budgeted rather than complete: when it stops, it says so.

SEE ALSO
  df(1), tree(1), stat(1)

EXAMPLES
  du
  du -d 1 /data
  du /data | sort -n -r | head -n 5

commands.title: echo - Print or write text
commands.description: Print text to stdout or redirect it to write a file.
commands.details:
NAME
  echo - Print and redirect messages.

SYNOPSIS
  echo <text>
  echo <text> > <file>

DESCRIPTION
  Prints a text string. If followed by the '>' redirection operator, writes the text to a file.

OPTIONS
  <text>
    The string to print or save.
  > <file>
    The path to write the output string to.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  The command line parser detects the redirection token '>'. In such cases, strips external quotation marks and dispatches a POST request to '/api/fs/write?path=<file>'.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Print or write completed.
  1
    Filesystem write error.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  cat(1), open(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  echo Hello user
  echo "THEME=dark" > /data/theme.cfg

commands.title: find - Find files recursively
commands.description: Recursively search for files matching a pattern under a path.
commands.details:
NAME
  find - Find files recursively.

SYNOPSIS
  find [path] -name <pattern>
  find <pattern>

DESCRIPTION
  Traverses the directory tree starting from the target directory. Matches names using a case-insensitive query.

OPTIONS
  [path]
    The starting folder (defaults to active CWD).
  -name <pattern>
    The filename query to match.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Issues recursive asynchronous HTTP requests to '/api/fs/list'. Triggers deep scanning on child folders and returns paths dynamically.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Traverse completed.
  1
    Filesystem scan error.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  ls(1), grep(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  find .txt
  find /data -name song.mp3

commands.title: free - Free memory
commands.description: Display how much free memory the device reports.
commands.details:
NAME
  free - Free memory.

SYNOPSIS
  free

DESCRIPTION
  Prints one line, 'free heap: <size>', with the free memory the device reports for its system. It is a single number: for detail and fragmentation use heap(1), on devices that support it. If the device does not report it, prints 'free: status unavailable'.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Reads the free_heap field of GET '/api/status'.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success.
  1
    Device unreachable or value not reported.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  status(1), uptime(1), heap(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  free

commands.title: gpio - Read or write a pin
commands.description: Raw pin I/O, within the set of pins the device allows. A pin outside that set is refused by the device with an error, surfaced verbatim. Which pins are allowed depends on the device.
commands.details:
NAME
  gpio - Read or write a pin

SYNOPSIS
  gpio read <pin>   |   gpio write <pin> <0|1>

DESCRIPTION
  Raw pin I/O, within the set of pins the device allows. A pin outside that set is refused by the device with an error, surfaced verbatim. Which pins are allowed depends on the device.

OPTIONS
  read PIN
    Read the pin level and print 'pin PIN = VALUE'. 'get' does the same.
  write PIN 0|1
    Set the level: 1 or high sets it high, any other value sets it low. 'set' does the same.

DEVICE COST
  One request to /api/gpio per call (GET to read, POST to write). Where there are user accounts it needs an administrator.

SEE ALSO
  ir(1), display(1)

EXAMPLES
  gpio read 1
  gpio write 2 1

commands.title: grep - Filter lines by pattern
commands.description: Search for a pattern in a file and output matching lines with numbers.
commands.details:
NAME
  grep - Search lines matching a pattern.

SYNOPSIS
  grep <pattern> <file>

DESCRIPTION
  Scans the file line by line for exact (case-sensitive) substring matches.

OPTIONS
  <pattern>
    The string query to search for.
  <file>
    The path of the target file to scan.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  The client fetches the target payload via GET '/api/fs/read'. It parses the payload in local memory, splits lines using a '\r?\n' regular expression, and applies 'String.prototype.includes()' to isolate matches. Renders results prefixed with their line numbers.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Scan completed.
  1
    File read failure or parser exception.
  404
    The specified file was not found.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  cat(1), find(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  grep SSID /system/config/settings.json
  grep ERROR /data/logs.txt

commands.title: head - Show first lines of a file
commands.description: Output the first part (default 10 lines) of a file.
commands.details:
NAME
  head - Output first lines of a file.

SYNOPSIS
  head [-n <lines>] <file>

DESCRIPTION
  Prints the initial segment of a file (defaults to 10 lines).

OPTIONS
  -n <lines>
    Specify the exact count of lines to print (e.g. '-n 5').
  <file>
    The target file path.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Downloads file contents via GET '/api/fs/read'. Parses lines in memory and isolates the top elements using array slicing ('slice(0, n)').

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success.
  1
    Read error or invalid parameter formatting.
  404
    Target file not found.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  tail(1), cat(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  head logs.txt
  head -n 5 /data/settings.json

commands.title: heap - Heap detail, including fragmentation
commands.description: Prints the internal, DMA and default heap pools with their free bytes, largest free block, minimum ever seen and fragmentation percentage, plus the HTTP server's minimum free stack.
commands.details:
NAME
  heap - Heap detail, including fragmentation

SYNOPSIS
  heap

DESCRIPTION
  Prints the internal, DMA and default heap pools with their free bytes, largest free block, minimum ever seen and fragmentation percentage, plus the HTTP server's minimum free stack.

OPTIONS
  This command takes no options.

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/heap.

NOTES
  Fragmentation, not free bytes, is the documented bottleneck on this chip — and free(1) cannot show it.

SEE ALSO
  free(1), diag(1), cpu(1), watch(1)

EXAMPLES
  heap
  watch -n 5 heap
  heap | grep frag

commands.title: hexdump - Hex and ASCII of the first bytes of a file
commands.description: Prints a classic hex dump: offset, sixteen bytes in hexadecimal, then the printable characters between pipes. It is how you look at an .ir capture, a firmware image or a save blob without cat turning it into mojibake.
commands.details:
NAME
  hexdump - Hex and ASCII of the first bytes of a file

SYNOPSIS
  hexdump [-n bytes] [-s offset] <file>

DESCRIPTION
  Prints a classic hex dump: offset, sixteen bytes in hexadecimal, then the printable characters between pipes. It is how you look at an .ir capture, a firmware image or a save blob without cat turning it into mojibake.

OPTIONS
  -n N
    How many bytes to read (default 256, maximum 4096).
  -s N
    Start at byte N.
  <file>
    The file to read.

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/fs/read with an HTTP Range header: where the device honours it, only the requested bytes travel (256 by default), even from a 640 MB file.

SEE ALSO
  cat(1), base64(1), wc(1)

EXAMPLES
  hexdump /data/remote.ir
  hexdump -n 64 -s 512 /data/image.bin

commands.title: history - Command history list
commands.description: List previous commands entered in the current session.
commands.details:
NAME
  history - Command history list.

SYNOPSIS
  history

DESCRIPTION

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Reads from the global 'hist' array stored in RAM. The queue is bounded to a maximum of 100 commands.

EXIT CODES

CONFORMING TO

AUTHOR

ADVANCED EXAMPLES

commands.title: ir - Drive the infrared LED
commands.synopsis: ir db | send <proto> <addr> <cmd> [rep] | raw <us,…> | tvbgone start|stop|status
commands.description: db prints the GPIO, the protocols this build encodes and the size of the TV-B-Gone table, so you can see what is possible before sending anything. send transmits one decoded code, raw transmits a timing list.
commands.details:
NAME
  ir - Drive the infrared LED

SYNOPSIS
  ir db | send <proto> <addr> <cmd> [rep] | raw <us,…> | tvbgone start|stop|status

DESCRIPTION
  db prints the GPIO, the protocols this build encodes and the size of the TV-B-Gone table, so you can see what is possible before sending anything. send transmits one decoded code, raw transmits a timing list.

OPTIONS
  db
    Show the capabilities (the default).
  send <proto> <addr> <cmd> [rep]
    Send a code.
  raw <us,…>
    Send raw microsecond timings.
  tvbgone start|stop|status
    Run the TV-B-Gone sweep.

DEVICE COST
  One request each.

NOTES
  Needs the device.ir permission. The jammer is deliberately not exposed here: it floods the band from a background task with no dry run, so it stays in the IR Remote app, where a visible button can stop it.

SEE ALSO
  display(1), link(1)

EXAMPLES
  ir db
  ir send nec 4 8
  ir tvbgone status

commands.description: Asks the shell to close an app window, freeing its RAM. Named by id (the one ps prints), not by the synthetic PID.
commands.details:

SYNOPSIS

DESCRIPTION

commands.description: Without an argument it prints the active language and its generation counter. With one it sets the language for the whole OS, including the native panel UI.

  lang - Read or set the OS display language

SYNOPSIS
  lang [it|en|fr|es|de]

DESCRIPTION

OPTIONS

commands.title: link - Show the ESP-NOW neighbours and the transfer state
commands.description: peers lists the devices this one can see over ESP-NOW, with the local name and channel; status shows whether a transfer is running and how far along it is.
commands.details:
NAME
  link - Show the ESP-NOW neighbours and the transfer state

SYNOPSIS
  link peers | link status

DESCRIPTION
  peers lists the devices this one can see over ESP-NOW, with the local name and channel; status shows whether a transfer is running and how far along it is.

OPTIONS
  peers
    List the neighbours (the default).
  status
    Show the transfer state.

DEVICE COST
  One GET each.

NOTES
  Needs the mesh.peer permission. Read-only on purpose: sending a command to another device turns a typo into someone else's problem, and the confirmation step for that lives in the Vicino app.

  link status

commands.title: ls - List directory contents
commands.description: List the folders and files in the current directory or under a given path.
commands.details:
NAME
  ls - List directory contents.

SYNOPSIS
  ls [path]

DESCRIPTION
  Lists the entries of the given folder in the device's storage. Without a path it lists the current working directory (CWD).
  Folders come first (highlighted, with a trailing slash '/'), then files with their size; each group is sorted alphabetically. The last line counts the items; an empty folder prints "(empty)". At most 200 entries are shown, and a longer listing says so.
  On devices that provide /proc, 'ls /proc' lists the nodes with live system information; read them with cat.

OPTIONS
  [path]
    The relative or absolute path of the folder to list.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  The listing goes through the system file layer, which asks the device with GET /api/fs/list?path=<path>. The same command works on every device.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. The folder exists and its contents were printed.
  1
    The folder does not exist, the device is not paired, or the file API cannot be reached.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  cd(1), find(1), pwd(1), tree(1), stat(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  ls               # List the current directory
  ls /data         # List the contents of the data folder
  ls ../system     # List using a relative path to the parent

commands.title: man - Online command manual
commands.description: Display the manual page of a Terminal command.
commands.details:
NAME
  man - Online manual pages.

SYNOPSIS
  man <command>

DESCRIPTION
  Shows the UNIX-style manual page of a Terminal command: a line with the name and synopsis, then the description and the details.
  The page comes from the manual that ships with the system, the same one the Help app shows, in the language the system is set to (Italian, English, Spanish, French or German). A command that manual does not cover is looked up among the device's own pages, in /system/registry/manual. Without an argument, man asks which page you want.

OPTIONS
  <command>
    The name of the command whose page to show.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Looks first in the manual built into the web OS, then reads the file /system/registry/manual/<command>.info from the device. If neither has the page, man prints "No manual entry for <command>".

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  help(1), clear(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  man ls
  man cd

commands.title: mkdir - Create directory
commands.description: Create a new folder at the given path, with any missing parent folders.
commands.details:
NAME
  mkdir - Create directory.

SYNOPSIS
  mkdir <dir>

DESCRIPTION
  Creates the folder in the device's storage and, like 'mkdir -p', any missing parent folders along the path. A folder that already exists is not an error. On success it prints "created <path>".

OPTIONS
  <dir>
    The relative or absolute path of the folder to create.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Goes through the system file layer, which sends POST /api/fs/mkdir?path=<dir> for each level that does not exist yet.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Folder created or already there.
  1
    Creation failed (e.g. storage full or read-only, permission denied, device not paired, or file API unreachable).

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  touch(1), rm(1), ls(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  mkdir /data/test
  mkdir new_notes
  mkdir /data/projects/2026/notes   # also creates the missing parents

commands.title: mv - Move or rename file
commands.description: Move or rename a file from source to destination.
commands.details:
NAME
  mv - Move or rename file.

SYNOPSIS
  mv <source> <dest>

DESCRIPTION
  Moves a file from the source path to the destination path. Renames the file if the parent directory remains the same.

OPTIONS
  <source>
    The target file to move.
  <dest>
    The destination path.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Executes a transactional sequence:
  1. Fetches source payload in RAM via GET '/api/fs/read'.
  2. Writes the payload to destination via POST '/api/fs/write'.
  3. If write returns HTTP 200, sends a POST to '/api/fs/delete' targeting the source file.
  This sequence prevents data loss during write faults.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. File moved successfully.
  1
    Write or deletion failure.
  404
    Source file was not found.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  cp(1), rm(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  mv old.txt new.txt
  mv /data/temp.txt /system/config/saved.txt

commands.title: notify - Post a notification to the OS notification centre
commands.description: How a long watch tells you it finished after you have switched to another window.
commands.details:
NAME
  notify - Post a notification to the OS notification centre

SYNOPSIS
  notify <text>

DESCRIPTION
  How a long watch tells you it finished after you have switched to another window.

OPTIONS
  <text>
    The message; without it, read standard input.

DEVICE COST
  None on the device: it goes through the shell's capability broker.

NOTES
  Needs the system.notify permission.

SEE ALSO
  watch(1), say(1)

EXAMPLES
  notify "the copy is done"

commands.title: open - Open file with default app
commands.description: Open a file using the associated graphical application.
commands.details:
NAME
  open - Open file with default application.

SYNOPSIS
  open <file>

DESCRIPTION
  Opens the specified resource. The desktop shell resolves the file extension and launches the default associated window.

OPTIONS
  <file>
    The path of the file to open.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Uses browser iframe 'postMessage' calls. Terminal sends '{ type: "open-file", path: file }' to the parent window. The shell parses the extension, reads '/system/config/file-associations.json' and opens the app (e.g. 'notepad', 'photo-viewer').

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Message dispatched to the shell.
  1
    Shell host unreachable or invalid file association.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS proprietary extension.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  echo(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  open /data/Pictures/wallpaper.png
  open /data/document.txt

commands.title: ota - Show the running slot, the next slot and the rollback state
commands.description: The thing to read before and after an update: which installed copy of the system (slot) is running, which one the next update would go to, the state of the current copy, and whether automatic return to the previous version (rollback) is on.
commands.details:
NAME
  ota - Show the running slot, the next slot and the rollback state

SYNOPSIS
  ota [status]

DESCRIPTION
  The thing to read before and after an update: which installed copy of the system (slot) is running, which one the next update would go to, the state of the current copy, and whether automatic return to the previous version (rollback) is on.
  It prints a single line: running <slot>  next <slot>  state <state>  rollback on|off. A field the device does not report is shown as '?'.

OPTIONS
  status
    The only accepted argument; it is also the default. Any other argument is refused with an error.

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/status.

NOTES
  Installing an update is deliberately NOT possible here: the device restarts as soon as an update is written, so a mistyped path recalled from history would be an irreversible update one keystroke away. Updates go through the system's own update procedure.

SEE ALSO
  status(1), reboot(1), diag(1)

EXAMPLES
  ota

commands.title: ping - Network latency diagnostics
commands.description: Measure the response time of the device or of a web host.
commands.details:
NAME
  ping - Test network latency.

SYNOPSIS
  ping [host]

DESCRIPTION
  Measures round-trip time (RTT) by sending 4 HTTP HEAD requests one after another, half a second apart. Without a host it measures the device itself (its /api/status route); with a host it measures that web server over HTTPS. At the end it prints how many replies arrived and the minimum, maximum and average time. Ctrl+C stops it.
  It is not an ICMP ping: the requests leave from the browser, so a host that does not answer over HTTPS, or that the browser blocks, counts as lost.

OPTIONS
  [host]
    The host name or URL to measure (e.g. 'google.com'); https:// is added when no scheme is given. If omitted, the device is measured.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Each request is timed in the browser with 'performance.now()', from sending to the answer, so the time covers the whole HTTP exchange, not just the network.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. At least one reply received.
  1
    All 4 requests were lost.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  curl(1), wget(1), status(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  ping             # Measure the device
  ping google.com  # Measure google.com

commands.title: ps - List apps as a process table
commands.description: Shows the installed, enabled apps with a run state. On a device that runs one foreground app plus the shell, this is the closest thing to a process list.
commands.details:

  ps - List apps as a process table

SYNOPSIS

commands.title: rm - Remove file or directory
commands.description: Permanently delete a file or an empty folder, without going through the Recycle Bin.
commands.details:
NAME
  rm - Remove file or directory.

SYNOPSIS
  rm <path>

DESCRIPTION
  Permanently deletes a file or an empty folder from the device's storage. The item does not go to the Recycle Bin and cannot be recovered. On success it prints "removed <path>". The /data folder itself cannot be removed.

OPTIONS
  <path>
    The file or empty folder to delete.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Goes through the system file layer, which sends POST /api/fs/delete?path=<path>. A folder that still contains anything is refused by the device.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Item deleted.
  1
    Deletion failed: the item does not exist, the folder is not empty, permission denied, device not paired, or file API unreachable.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  cp(1), mv(1), mkdir(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES

  rm /data/empty_dir

commands.title: say - Speak text through the device
commands.description: Sends text to the speech engine, either as an argument or from a pipe. Inside a pipeline it passes the text on, so a spoken line can still be recorded.
commands.details:
NAME
  say - Speak text through the device

SYNOPSIS
  say [text]

DESCRIPTION
  Sends text to the speech engine, either as an argument or from a pipe. Inside a pipeline it passes the text on, so a spoken line can still be recorded.

OPTIONS
  [text]
    What to say; without it, read standard input.

  One POST /api/tts.

NOTES

SEE ALSO
  notify(1), anima(1), clip(1)

  dmesg -l E | anima "what is wrong?" | say

commands.title: screen - Save what the screen is showing
commands.description: Captures what the device's screen is showing and saves it as a file in the device's storage. No other terminal has a subject to photograph.
commands.details:
NAME
  screen - Save what the screen is showing

SYNOPSIS
  screen [-o <file>]

DESCRIPTION
  Captures what the device's screen is showing and saves it as a file in the device's storage. No other terminal has a subject to photograph.

OPTIONS

SEE ALSO
  display(1), open(1)

  screen -o /data/shot.bmp

commands.title: sort - Sort standard input
commands.description: Reorders the lines that arrive from a pipe.
commands.details:
NAME
  sort - Sort standard input

SYNOPSIS
  sort [-r] [-n] [-u] [-k N]

  Reorders the lines that arrive from a pipe.

OPTIONS
  -r
    Reverse the order.

commands.title: stat - Show the type, size and lock state of one entry
commands.description: Reports what a single file or directory is, without listing the whole folder it lives in.
commands.details:
NAME
  stat - Show the type, size and lock state of one entry

SYNOPSIS
  stat <path>

DESCRIPTION
  Reports what a single file or directory is, without listing the whole folder it lives in. Prints the path, the type (file or dir), the size in bytes and in readable form ("-" for a directory) and whether the entry is protected.

OPTIONS
  <path>
    The file or directory to describe.

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/fs/stat on devices that offer it; on the others one GET /api/fs/list on the PARENT directory, from which stat picks the entry.

NOTES
  stat does not show a modification time: the "modified" line says the device does not report one, rather than inventing it.

SEE ALSO
  ls(1), du(1), tree(1)

EXAMPLES
  stat /data/notes.txt
  stat /apps/terminal

commands.title: status - Global system diagnostics
commands.description: Print the system version, uptime, free memory, storage, installed apps and network state.
commands.details:
NAME
  status - Diagnostic status.

SYNOPSIS
  status

DESCRIPTION
  Displays a summary of the device, one item per line: system name and version with the seconds of uptime, free memory (heap), storage (type, free and total space), number of installed apps and network (clock synced via NTP or not and, if present, the network name). Items the device does not report are left out.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  One GET to '/api/status'; the command formats the fields of the answer without further requests.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success.
  1
    Device unreachable.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS proprietary extension.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  uptime(1), free(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  status

commands.title: tail - Show last lines of a file
commands.description: Output the last part (default 10 lines) of a file.
commands.details:
NAME
  tail - Output last lines of a file.

SYNOPSIS
  tail [-n <lines>] <file>

DESCRIPTION
  Prints the trailing segment of a file (defaults to 10 lines).

OPTIONS
  -n <lines>
    Specify the exact count of lines to print (e.g. '-n 5').
  <file>
    The target file path.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Downloads file contents via GET '/api/fs/read'. Parses lines in memory and isolates the bottom elements using array slicing ('slice(allLines.length - n)').

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success.
  1
    Read error or invalid parameter formatting.
  404
    Target file not found.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  head(1), cat(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  tail logs.txt
  tail -n 3 /data/net.cfg

commands.title: tee - Write standard input to a file and pass it on
commands.description: Saves whatever flows through it and then hands the same text to the next stage, which is what makes a pipeline durable.
commands.details:
NAME
  tee - Write standard input to a file and pass it on

SYNOPSIS
  tee <file>

DESCRIPTION
  Saves whatever flows through it and then hands the same text to the next stage, which is what makes a pipeline durable.

OPTIONS
  <file>
    Where to write.

DEVICE COST
  Exactly one POST /api/fs/write.

SEE ALSO
  cat(1), clip(1), base64(1)

EXAMPLES
  diag | tee /data/diag.txt
  dmesg -l E | tee /data/errors.txt | wc

commands.title: theme - Change OS color theme
commands.description: Display or switch the system graphic theme (dark or light).
commands.details:
NAME
  theme - System graphic theme.

SYNOPSIS
  theme [dark|light]

DESCRIPTION
  With no argument, or with a value other than dark or light, prints the current theme and the usage. With dark or light it applies the theme to the Terminal at once and saves it in the system settings.

OPTIONS
  [dark|light]
    The theme name to apply.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Sets the 'data-theme' attribute of the page, then reads '/system/config/settings.json', updates the ui.theme entry and writes the file back through '/api/fs/write'. If saving fails, the theme stays applied in this window only and the command shows a warning.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success, also when the theme was applied only locally (with a warning).

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS proprietary extension.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  status(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  theme            # Read current theme
  theme light      # Switch to light theme
  theme dark       # Switch to dark theme

commands.title: touch - Create empty file
commands.description: Create a new empty file at the specified path, if it does not exist.
commands.details:
NAME
  touch - Initialize empty file.

SYNOPSIS
  touch <file>

DESCRIPTION
  Creates a file of zero bytes; missing folders along the path are created. If the file already exists, it is left untouched (content and date stay the same) and the command says so.

OPTIONS
  <file>
    The path of the file to initialize.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  First checks whether the file is there (with '/api/fs/stat' or the folder listing). Only if it is missing does it send a POST to '/api/fs/write' with an empty body, never overwriting. If the folder cannot be read, it reports the error and writes nothing.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. File created or already present.
  1
    Read or write error on the device's storage.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  mkdir(1), rm(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  touch /data/empty.txt

commands.title: tr - Translate or delete characters
commands.description: Replaces each character of set1 with the matching one in set2, or deletes them with -d. Sets are literal: no ranges or classes, to save bytes on the device.
commands.details:
NAME
  tr - Translate or delete characters

SYNOPSIS
  tr <set1> <set2>   |   tr -d <set>

DESCRIPTION
  Replaces each character of set1 with the matching one in set2, or deletes them with -d. Sets are literal: no ranges or classes, to save bytes on the device.

OPTIONS
  -d SET
    Delete every character in the set instead of translating.
  If set2 is shorter than set1, its last character fills the rest.

DEVICE COST
  none

SEE ALSO
  cut(1), sort(1)

EXAMPLES
  echo hello | tr aeiou _
  cat /data/f | tr -d \r

commands.title: tree - Print a directory tree
commands.description: Prints the subtree under a path, indented one level per depth, directories first and marked with a trailing slash.
commands.details:
NAME
  tree - Print a directory tree

SYNOPSIS
  tree [-L N] [path]

DESCRIPTION
  Prints the subtree under a path, indented one level per depth, directories first and marked with a trailing slash.

OPTIONS
  -L N
    Descend at most N levels (default 3, hard maximum 6).
  [path]
    Where to start; the working directory by default.

DEVICE COST
  The same budgeted walk du uses: one listing per directory, sequential, capped at 60 listings and 200 printed entries.

SEE ALSO
  ls(1), du(1), find(1)

EXAMPLES
  tree
  tree -L 1 /apps
  tree /data | grep .txt

commands.title: unalias - Remove an alias
commands.description: Deletes one alias and saves the list again.
commands.details:
NAME
  unalias - Remove an alias

SYNOPSIS
  unalias <name>

DESCRIPTION
  Deletes one alias and saves the list again.

OPTIONS
  <name>
    The alias to remove.

DEVICE COST
  One POST /api/fs/write.

SEE ALSO
  alias(1)

EXAMPLES
  unalias ll

commands.title: uname - System name, edition and version
commands.description: Print the operating system name; with -a also the edition and the version.
commands.details:
NAME
  uname - System information.

SYNOPSIS
  uname [-a]

DESCRIPTION
  Without options it prints the operating system name. With '-a' it prints on one line the name, the edition id the device reports and the system version.

OPTIONS
  -a
    Adds the edition and the version.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Reads the name and version from '/api/status' and the edition from the device capabilities ('/api/system/caps', or inferred from '/api/status' on devices without that route). If the device does not answer it uses the defaults (NucleoOS, 0.1.0) and leaves out the edition when it is not known.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Always: without an answer the command prints the defaults.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  status(1), uptime(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  uname
  uname -a

commands.title: uniq - Collapse repeated adjacent lines
commands.description: Turns a wall of identical log lines into one line, optionally with a count. This is the step that makes two kilobytes of dmesg small enough to hand to anima.
commands.details:
NAME
  uniq - Collapse repeated adjacent lines

SYNOPSIS
  uniq [-c]

DESCRIPTION
  Turns a wall of identical log lines into one line, optionally with a count. This is the step that makes two kilobytes of dmesg small enough to hand to anima.

OPTIONS
  -c
    Prefix each line with how many times it repeated.

DEVICE COST
  None. Entirely browser-side.

SEE ALSO
  sort(1), grep(1), anima(1)

EXAMPLES
  dmesg | sort | uniq -c | sort -n -r

commands.title: uptime - System active time
commands.description: Show how long the device has been running and how much free memory it has.
commands.details:
NAME
  uptime - System active time.

SYNOPSIS
  uptime

DESCRIPTION
  Prints the time elapsed since the device last started, in hours, minutes and seconds, and the free memory (heap) the device reports. Sample line: up 2h 15m 4s, heap free: ...

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Reads the uptime_s and free_heap fields from '/api/status'.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success.
  1
    Device unreachable.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  status(1), free(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  uptime

commands.title: verify - Grounded fact check against the on-device knowledge
commands.description: Asks ANIMA whether an asserted value for a key is confirmed, contradicted or unknown, and prints the evidence it used.
commands.details:
NAME
  verify - Grounded fact check against the on-device knowledge

SYNOPSIS
  verify <key> <asserted> [--kind fact|numeric] [-l it|en]

DESCRIPTION
  Asks ANIMA whether an asserted value for a key is confirmed, contradicted or unknown, and prints the evidence it used. The verdict and the evidence come out on one line, separated by a tab. The last word is the asserted value; all the words before it form the key.

OPTIONS
  <key>
    What is being asked about, e.g. "capital of france".
  <asserted>
    The value to check.
  --kind
    fact or numeric.
  -l
    Answer language (it or en).

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/anima/verify.

NOTES
  Works on devices that have ANIMA on board. On the others the command reports it as a warning, not as an error: "not available on this device", or "not available on this build" when the route answers 404.

SEE ALSO
  anima(1), diag(1)

EXAMPLES
  verify "capital of france" Lyon

commands.title: watch - Re-run a command in place every few seconds
commands.description: Runs a command repeatedly and redraws its output over the previous tick instead of scrolling the screen. It is the fragmentation microscope: watch -n5 heap.
commands.details:
NAME
  watch - Re-run a command in place every few seconds

SYNOPSIS
  watch [-n seconds] [-c count] <command>

DESCRIPTION
  Runs a command repeatedly and redraws its output over the previous tick instead of scrolling the screen. It is the fragmentation microscope: watch -n5 heap.

OPTIONS
  -n S
    Seconds between ticks (3 by default, never less than 2).
  -c N
    How many ticks (10 by default, 300 at most).

DEVICE COST
  Whatever the inner command costs, once per tick. Ticks never overlap, the interval is clamped to two seconds, and three consecutive failures stop it. Ctrl+C stops it immediately.

NOTES
  Refused inside a pipeline, and wifi scan refuses to run inside it: a blocking radio operation on a loop would knock the device off its own network.

SEE ALSO
  heap(1), diag(1), notify(1)

EXAMPLES
  watch -n 5 heap
  watch -n 10 -c 60 status

commands.title: wc - Word, line, and byte count
commands.description: Print word, line, and byte counts of a file.
commands.details:
NAME
  wc - Word, line, and byte count.

SYNOPSIS
  wc <file>

DESCRIPTION
  Performs a metrics analysis of the target file, printing line, word, and byte counts.

OPTIONS
  <file>
    The target file to parse.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  Fetches data via the filesystem read endpoint. Lines are resolved using a '\n' split, words using a '\s+' regex filter, and bytes using a JavaScript 'Blob' size check.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Counts printed.
  1
    Filesystem read error.
  404
    File was not found.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  cat(1), head(1), tail(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  wc /data/notes.txt

commands.title: wget - Download file from web
commands.description: Download a file from a URL and save it to the device's storage.
commands.details:
NAME
  wget - Download file over HTTP.

SYNOPSIS
  wget <url> [-O <destination_file>]

DESCRIPTION
  Downloads a resource with a GET request and writes it to the device's storage. Without -O the file is named after the last part of the URL (without the query string), or 'downloaded_file', and lands in the current directory. A URL without a scheme is treated as https://.

OPTIONS
  <url>
    The URL of the file to download.
  -O <destination_file>
    Path of the file to save the resource to. An existing file is replaced.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
  The download is made by the browser, so its CORS rules apply: a site that does not allow it fails with 'network error or CORS blocked'. The data is then sent via POST to '/api/fs/write'; missing folders are created.

EXIT CODES
  0
    Success. Downloaded and written successfully.
  1
    Network error, failed HTTP response or write error.

CONFORMING TO
  NucleoOS extension compatible with POSIX.

AUTHOR
  NucleoOS Core Devs.

SEE ALSO
  curl(1), ping(1)

ADVANCED EXAMPLES
  wget example.com/index.html
  wget http://example.com/file.bin -O /data/file.bin

commands.title: which - Say whether a name is a builtin, an alias or an app
commands.description: Answers the question "is that a command or an app" in one line.
commands.details:
NAME
  which - Say whether a name is a builtin, an alias or an app

SYNOPSIS
  which <name>

DESCRIPTION
  Answers the question "is that a command or an app" in one line.

OPTIONS
  <name>
    The name to look up.

DEVICE COST
  One GET /api/apps, memoised for 30 s and shared with the apps command.

SEE ALSO
  apps(1), alias(1), man(1)

EXAMPLES
  which ls
  which notepad

commands.title: wifi - Scan, join, forget and prioritise networks
commands.synopsis: wifi scan | known | join <ssid> [pass] | forget <ssid> | prio <ssid> <n> | reconnect
commands.description: The radio, from a shell. scan lists what is in the air with signal, channel and security; known lists the saved networks and marks the current one with an asterisk; the rest change them.
commands.details:
NAME
  wifi - Scan, join, forget and prioritise networks

SYNOPSIS
  wifi scan | known | join <ssid> [pass] | forget <ssid> | prio <ssid> <n> | reconnect

DESCRIPTION
  The radio, from a shell. scan lists what is in the air with signal, channel and security; known lists the saved networks and marks the current one with an asterisk; the rest change them.

OPTIONS
  scan
    List visible networks.
  known
    List saved networks (the default).
  join <ssid> [pass]
    Connect and save.
  forget <ssid>
    Delete a saved network.
  prio <ssid> <n>
    Set the join priority.
  reconnect
    Reconnect now.

DEVICE COST
  One request each. scan is a BLOCKING radio operation, so it is rate limited to once per ten seconds and refused inside watch.

NOTES
  Needs the net.wifi permission. A password typed inline is not stored in the shell history.

SEE ALSO
  status(1), ping(1), link(1)

EXAMPLES
  wifi scan
  wifi known
  wifi join home-wifi secret
  wifi scan | sort -k2 -n
